title.description: what the chart shows, with no period or year: 'Aid to Kenya by donor'. make_charts adds the period the card shows, and refuses a title naming a year the frame covers
title.title: Title

type.description: line_chart: a series over time, or up to 8 places over time as one chart with the place dimension listing them; bar_chart: places or categories compared at one period; stat_card: one headline value; table: the detail. A chart shows every period its frame covers. A frame whose rows all cover one period (a collapsed window such as 2020/2024) has no run of periods to draw as a line: show it as a bar_chart, a table or a stat_card. A facet dimension (provenance, unit, measurementMethod) holding several values in the frame's view is bound to one of them in select_json, whatever the type.
type.title: Type

Chart.title: Chart

function_declarations.description:
Ask the user one to three questions before going on, with the likely
answers to each. The user sees them together in one pause and answers
each by picking an option, writing their own answer, or leaving it to
you.

Ask only what changes the answer. Each question offers at least one
option. An option for one of a part's candidates carries the spec_id
the search result gives it, and the answer names that spec_id when
the user picks it. Each spec_id goes on one option. A prices question
names its part in `prices_of`, and its options are filled in. End
your turn after calling ask_user. Every answer comes back as this
call's result.
function_declarations.name: ask_user

AskOption.description: One answer `ask_user` offers: its wording and, for a part's candidate, its spec_id.

label.description: the answer as the user reads it
label.title: Label

spec_id.description: for one of a part's candidates, the spec_id the search result gives it; leave it out for any other answer
spec_id.title: Spec Id

AskOption.title: AskOption

AskQuestion.description: One question `ask_user` puts to the user, with the answers it offers.

options.description: the likely answers, at least one; the user may also write their own. Leave it empty for a prices question, whose options are filled in for you
options.title: Options

prices_of.description: for the prices question of a part that lists `open_prices`, that part's spec_id
prices_of.title: Prices Of

question.description: the question as the user reads it
question.title: Question

AskQuestion.title: AskQuestion

function_declarations.description:
Hand a question to the planner, which builds a plan that
constructs the answer from the data. The user approves the plan
before it runs.

`brief` is the whole question in full: every measure and place, and
the period the user named. When the user named none, say so, with
the year you chose if you chose one. The years a source holds are
not the question's period. `asks` lists each output the user asked
for, one per entry, in the user's terms: a number, a ranking, a
chart, a comparison; at least one and at most six, each one short line. One figure
the user asked for across several years is an ask of its own that
sets `across_years`: "the total between 2010 and the latest" is one
cumulative number beside the yearly figures. A view added to help
read the answer is not an ask. The planner answers or declines each
ask, so an output left off the list can drop out of the plan
unnoticed.
Each ask is `{"text", "by", "over", "across_years"}`. Every party a
search this turn held open goes in some ask's `by` or `over`, and the
plan keeps the parties each ask lists in `by` together in one output.
End your turn after calling it; the plan's result comes back as this
call's result.
function_declarations.name: plan

AskedOutput.description:
One output the user asked for, the parties it lists one by one, and
those it totals across.

across_years.description: true when the user asked for this output as one figure, or one ranking, taken across several years: a total, an average, a peak or a low over them ("the total between 2015 and 2022", "in total, over all years", "the year aid peaked"). It permits the plan to combine the years and requires nothing. Leave it false for a figure for each year and for one year, and for a total or a ranking when the user named no years: the years a source holds are not a span the user asked for
across_years.title: Across Years

by.description: each party the output lists one by one, in the words search takes as open_roles: ["creditor"] for "debt service by creditor"; empty for a total or a figure about named parties. Parties listed together are shown together in one output; an output per party is an ask per party
by.title: By

over.description: each party the output totals across into one figure: ["donor"] for "total aid from all donors". Such a party stays out of open_roles, and the search call names the population as an entity
over.title: Over

text.description: the output in the user's terms, one short line
text.title: Text

AskedOutput.title: AskedOutput

Load a skill a search result named: the definitions, caveats and
methods an answer in its domain rests on. Returns the first page of
the skill's text and the files it links, or with `path` one of those
files, a page at a time.

digest.description: The digest a closing line names, on a continuation.
digest.title: Digest

offset.description: Where a page starts: 0, or the offset a closing line names.
offset.title: Offset

path.description: A file's path exactly as the list gives it, or SKILL.md. A file refused as not found is not retried under a guessed path.
path.title: Path

skill_id.description: The id of a skill a search result named.

function_declarations.description:
What the Development Finance Observatory is and what this assistant
can do, in general. Whether DFO has data on a topic or a measure is
a data question, answered by searching for it. Returns DFO's own
description and `counts`, its whole-catalogue totals; quote a count
only from `counts`. Or returns an error saying why the description
could not be read, which you pass on plainly.
function_declarations.name: explain_dfo

function_declarations.description:
Read back, in full, what an earlier turn of this conversation did:
every source and decision of a plan, what a search read, or the
user's canvas.

`part`: "plan" for the plan records of a turn, "readings" for the
search readings of a turn, "canvas" for the conversation's cards, or,
with `component_id`, that one card's stored entry. The canvas listing
ranks cards by the turn that drew them and holds no card's place on
the canvas. Each card it lists names its `turn`:
- `blocks`: cards in full with their facts, while places remain:
  this turn's cards on the canvas, then the pinned ones, then the
  other cards on the canvas, newest turn first.
- `titles`: the next cards of those three groups, by id, title and
  type.
- `off_canvas`: cards off the canvas by id, title and type, a whole
  turn at a time, this turn's first, then newest turn first.
- `counted`: for each turn with cards no list holds, how many are on
  the canvas (`on_canvas`) and how many off it (`off_canvas`).
- `counted_rest`: the same two counts for older turns' cards and
  cards of no recorded turn.
For a plan or readings, `turn` is the turn's number as the
conversation digest counts them; leave it out for the newest turn
that has the part. A target that does not exist is refused with the
values that do.
function_declarations.name: recall

function_declarations.description:
Take cards off the user's canvas, when the conversation has moved to
another subject or the user asks for cards to go.

`component_ids` names the cards to take off, by the component ids the
canvas lists; set `all_cards` to take off every card the user has
not pinned. A pinned card stays on the canvas, since only the user
unpins it. Returns the ids taken off and, as `kept_pinned`, the
pinned cards left in place, with each one's title under `titles`; a
named card already off the canvas
needs nothing and is named back as `already_off`, and an id this
conversation never held is named back as `not_in_conversation`. When
nothing came off, `note` says what each named id met.
function_declarations.name: remove_cards
